requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1.
requirements.summary: UFW was enabled with a default-deny incoming policy, remained active and enabled after a demonstrated reboot, and retained the same persisted rule-file checksum and ordered rules.

requirements.requirement: Allow SSH to node1 from any address.
requirements.summary: Final IPv4 and IPv6 rules allow TCP 22 from anywhere. After node1's reboot, SSH banners were obtained from both node2 and node3, and the final state showed SSH active.

requirements.requirement: Allow TCP port 9000 only from node2, while rejecting node3 and every other source.
requirements.summary: The ordered final rules allow node2's IPv4 address before IPv4/IPv6 catch-all rejects. With a live listener, node2 received HTTP 200 and node3 was actively refused both before and after node1's reboot. However, a direct test from node1 itself—also a non-node2 source—successfully connected, contradicting the literal requirement to reject every other source.

overall_summary: The persistent UFW firewall and global SSH allowance are fully demonstrated, including survival of a real node1 reboot. Port 9000 behaves correctly for node2 and node3 and has an appropriate catch-all rule, but the captured successful connection from node1 itself prevents the literal “only from node2/everywhere else rejected” outcome from being fully satisfied. Mandatory restart evidence is coherent and complete across all managed nodes.
limitations: The evidence directly tests port 9000 from node2, node3, and node1 itself, but not from an additional external IPv4 source or any IPv6 source; coverage of those sources relies on the displayed catch-all rules.

The successful node1 self-connection may reflect local-host/loopback handling rather than externally routed ingress, but the public instruction does not exempt node1-originated traffic, so it remains a material contradiction.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. Firewall changes directly implemented the task; generating missing SSH host keys and recovering SSH supported required SSH behavior verification; temporary port-9000 listeners and files were bounded evidence fixtures and were removed; and all reboots served the mandatory restart protocol. Final observations show no port-9000 listener, no failed services, healthy package state, and no abandoned test files. The restart protocol is strong for all three nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered system/network or task behavior.
